'''RefDiff''' (''The Ref-Differentiator'') is a [[Gadgets|user script]] for MediaWiki's diff view ({{mono|Special:Diff}}). It decouples inline citation templates from prose in the diff table, eliminating '''"template camouflage"''' so reviewers can focus on text changes.

== The Problem: Template Camouflage ==

Quality control, vandalism patrolling, and editorial review on Wikipedia happen primarily in the diff view ({{mono|Special:Diff}}).

When an article uses standard inline citations ({{tag|ref|content={{tlx|cite book |author&#61;... |title&#61;...}}}}), references often contain extensive bibliographic parameters. When an editor edits a single word in a sentence, standard MediaWiki diffs ({{mono|wikidiff2}}) highlight the entire paragraph as modified:

{| class="wikitable" style="width: 100%; table-layout: fixed; font-family: monospace; font-size: 0.9em;"
! style="width: 50%; background: #eaecf0; text-align: left; padding: 6px 10px;" | Line 42 (Old):
! style="width: 50%; background: #eaecf0; text-align: left; padding: 6px 10px;" | Line 42 (New):
|-
| style="vertical-align: top; background: #ffe6e6; padding: 8px 10px; line-height: 1.5;" |
<span style="font-weight: bold; color: #b32424; margin-right: 6px;">−</span> The atmosphere consists of carbon dioxide&lt;ref&gt;<nowiki>{{Cite book |author=Schmidt, Rainer |title=Planetary Atmospheres |year=2020 |pages=112–</nowiki><del style="background: #ffb3b3; color: #7a0000; font-weight: bold; text-decoration: line-through; padding: 1px 3px; border-radius: 2px;">115</del><nowiki> |isbn=978-3-12-345678-9}}</nowiki>&lt;/ref&gt;, creating an <del style="background: #ffb3b3; color: #7a0000; font-weight: bold; text-decoration: line-through; padding: 1px 3px; border-radius: 2px;">extreme</del> greenhouse effect.
| style="vertical-align: top; background: #e6ffe6; padding: 8px 10px; line-height: 1.5;" |
<span style="font-weight: bold; color: #14866d; margin-right: 6px;">+</span> The atmosphere consists of carbon dioxide&lt;ref&gt;<nowiki>{{Cite book |author=Schmidt, Rainer |title=Planetary Atmospheres |year=2020 |pages=112–</nowiki><ins style="background: #a3f0a3; color: #006600; font-weight: bold; text-decoration: none; padding: 1px 3px; border-radius: 2px;">125</ins><nowiki> |isbn=978-3-12-345678-9}}</nowiki>&lt;/ref&gt;, creating a <ins style="background: #a3f0a3; color: #006600; font-weight: bold; text-decoration: none; padding: 1px 3px; border-radius: 2px;">runaway</ins> greenhouse effect.
|}

=== Why this is harmful: ===
# '''Camouflaged Vandalism:''' Subtle vandalism (changing numbers, swapping years, altering names) hides inside the visual noise of untouched template parameters.
# '''Misleading Diffs on Citation Fixes:''' Updating a dead URL or correcting a page number marks the entire surrounding paragraph as modified, misleading patrollers into thinking text was rewritten.
# '''Reviewer Fatigue:''' Patrollers waste significant cognitive energy mentally filtering template syntax.

== How RefDiff Works ==

RefDiff runs client-side in the browser and transforms the diff table in-place:

# '''Zero Loss:''' Fully preserves Wikipedia's native diff table (line numbers, revision headers, context rows, and the native {{mono|Inline}} checkbox).
# '''Clean Prose Diffs:''' Inline {{tag|ref}} tags and footnote templates (such as {{tlx|sfn}}, {{tlx|r}}, {{tlx|efn}}, and {{tlx|harvnb}}) are replaced with clean, unobtrusive mathematical angle-bracket badges (e.g. {{mono|⟨ref1⟩}}, {{mono|⟨~ref2~⟩}}, or scholarly author-year badges like {{mono|⟨Reichert & Wolfram 2010⟩}}).
# '''Dedicated Citation Rows:''' If a citation was modified, added, or removed, RefDiff inserts an isolated citation diff row directly underneath the sentence.
# '''Automatic Context Conversion:''' If an edit ''only'' touched citation metadata, the prose line automatically converts to context appearance (calm gray, no diff markers). Patrollers instantly know the text itself was not altered.
# '''Interactive Reference Links & Hover Previews:''' Badges are rendered as standard footnote links ({{tag|sup|params=class="reference"|content=&lt;a href="..."&gt;}}). Hovering over any badge displays Wikipedia's standard '''Reference Preview hovercard''' (from Read mode), and clicking modified/added citations jumps directly to their citation diff row below.

== Visual Guide & Badge Legend ==

RefDiff uses mathematical angle brackets ({{mono|⟨...⟩}}) to avoid syntactic collisions with external links ({{mono|[...]}}) and wikilinks ({{mono|<nowiki>[[...]]</nowiki>}}):

{| class="wikitable"
! Badge !! Meaning !! Appearance !! Reviewer Action
|-
| {{mono|⟨ref1⟩}} / {{mono|⟨Castritius 2005⟩}}
| '''Unmodified Reference'''
| Subtle neutral gray text, normal weight
| '''Ignore:''' Identical on both sides; zero prose distraction.
|-
| {{mono|⟨~ref2~⟩}} / {{mono|⟨~Voyles 1992~⟩}}
| '''Modified Reference / Shortened Footnote'''
| Amber highlight, bold, hover tooltip
| '''Review:''' Bibliographic metadata or page parameters changed; see citation row below.
|-
| {{mono|⟨+ref3+⟩}} / {{mono|⟨+Reichert & Wolfram 2010+⟩}}
| '''Added Reference / Shortened Footnote'''
| Crisp green badge, bold
| '''Verify:''' New source added to the claim.
|-
| {{mono|⟨-ref4-⟩}} / {{mono|⟨-Smith 2018-⟩}}
| '''Removed Reference / Shortened Footnote'''
| Crisp red badge, bold, strikethrough
| '''Verify:''' Source removed from the claim.
|}

=== Shortened Footnotes & Citation Templates ===

In addition to standard {{tag|ref}} tags, RefDiff natively parses Wikipedia footnote templates:
* '''Shortened Footnotes:''' {{tlx|sfn}}, {{tlx|sfnp}}, {{tlx|sfnm}}, {{tlx|sfnmp}}
* '''Shorthand References:''' {{tlx|r}}
* '''Explanatory Footnotes:''' {{tlx|efn}}, {{tlx|efn-la}}, etc.
* '''Harvard Citations:''' {{tlx|harv}}, {{tlx|harvnb}}, {{tlx|harvtxt}}, {{tlx|harvp}}

For shortened footnotes, RefDiff automatically synthesizes author names and publication years into clean scholarly badges (e.g. {{mono|⟨Castritius 2005⟩}}, {{mono|⟨Reichert & Wolfram 2010⟩}}, or {{mono|⟨Author et al. 2023⟩}}). Page numbers (such as {{mono|p=574}}) are cleanly separated into the decoupled citation diff row below, while the badge itself links directly to the generated {{mono|cite_note-FOOTNOTE*}} anchor in the article references for instant native hovercard previews.

== Installation ==

=== Option 1: English Wikipedia (Recommended) ===
Add the following line to your local [[Special:MyPage/common.js|common.js]] page on English Wikipedia:

<syntaxhighlight lang="javascript">
// [[m:User:Powercycler/refdiff.js]] - RefDiff: Decoupled citation diffs for Special:Diff
mw.loader.load('https://meta.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=User:Powercycler/refdiff.js&action=raw&ctype=text/javascript');
</syntaxhighlight>

=== Option 2: Global Cross-Wiki Installation (All Wikimedia Wikis) ===
To enable RefDiff automatically across all language Wikipedias, Wikidata, and Wikimedia projects at once, add the exact same line to your central **[[:m:Special:MyPage/global.js|global.js on Meta-Wiki]]**:

<syntaxhighlight lang="javascript">
// [[m:User:Powercycler/refdiff.js]] - RefDiff across all wikis
mw.loader.load('https://meta.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=User:Powercycler/refdiff.js&action=raw&ctype=text/javascript');
</syntaxhighlight>

=== Option 3: Personal Copy / Developer Fork ===
If you maintain your own custom script fork at [[:m:Special:MyPage/refdiff.js|m:Special:MyPage/refdiff.js]], load it dynamically with:

<syntaxhighlight lang="javascript">
// [[m:Special:MyPage/refdiff.js]] - Load personal Meta-Wiki fork
mw.loader.load('//meta.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=User:' + encodeURIComponent((mw.config.get('wgUserName') || '').replace(/ /g, '_')) + '/refdiff.js&action=raw&ctype=text/javascript');
</syntaxhighlight>

Then bypass your browser cache (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>F5</kbd> on Windows/Linux, <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>R</kbd> on macOS).

== UI Controls & Mode Switching ==

=== Native OOUI Mode Switcher ===
On Vector 2022 and Vector legacy, RefDiff adds a button directly to Wikipedia's native diff mode selector, accompanied by an in-toolbar toggle placed to the left:

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align: center;"
| {{mono|[  Inline modified refs]}} || {{mono|[ 👁 Visual ]}} || {{mono|[ <nowiki>[[]]</nowiki> Wikitext ]}} || {{mono|'''[ ⧉ RefDiff ]'''}} || {{mono|Inline ( )}}
|}

* '''In-Toolbar Inline Toggle:''' An {{mono|[ ] Inline modified refs}} checkbox is placed directly to the left of the mode bar (unchecked by default). Keeping it to the left prevents layout shift and UI jumps on page load. Checking it instantly keeps modified references inline in prose with a prepended {{mono|⟨~label~⟩}} badge without creating rows below, while added and deleted references always decouple into separate rows.
* '''Three-Way Diff Mode Switching:''' Seamlessly switches between {{mono|Visual}} (native rich HTML diff), standard {{mono|Wikitext}} diff, and decoupled {{mono|RefDiff}} instantly, with no page reload.
* '''Visual Diff Interoperability:''' Switching to {{mono|Visual}} cleanly dismisses citation diff rows and restores native diff markup; switching back to {{mono|RefDiff}} seamlessly re-engages citation decoupling.
* '''State Persistence:''' Remembers your latest mode selection across diff pages via {{mono|mw.storage}}. If you toggle back to Wikitext or open a diff in Visual mode, diffs remain in your chosen view until you click RefDiff again.
* '''Inline Switch Inactive during RefDiff:''' The native {{mono|Inline}} toggle switch is automatically disabled and inactive while RefDiff is active to preserve two-column citation alignment, and automatically re-enabled when switching back to standard Wikitext diff.
* '''Fallback Mode Bar:''' On older skins without the OOUI button container (e.g. Monobook), RefDiff displays a clean switcher bar above the diff table:
  : {{mono|[ ] Inline modified refs • Diff view: '''Decoupled (RefDiff)''' • Standard Wikidiff}}

== Configuration & Options ==

RefDiff supports configurable decoupling modes to tailor review workflows to personal editor preferences:

=== Decouple Rows vs. Inline Modified Mode ===
By default, all reference edits—modified, added, and deleted citations—are decoupled into dedicated {{mono|tr.refdiff-cit-row}} rows below the prose line. If you prefer to keep citation modifications directly inline inside prose while still shortening unchanged citations into hoverable badges and still isolating added/deleted citations into separate rows, you can toggle the inline preference:

* '''Interactive In-Toolbar Toggle:''' Check {{mono|[✓] Inline modified refs}} right in the toolbar above the diff table. The table instantly refreshes in-place.
* '''In your {{mono|common.js}}''' (before loading {{mono|refdiff.js}}):
  <syntaxhighlight lang="javascript">
  window.refdiffConfig = {
      inlineModified: true // Keep modified citations inline via ⟨~label~⟩ badge; shorten unchanged citations into hoverable badges; added & deleted citations always separate
  };
  </syntaxhighlight>
* '''Per-Diff URL Parameter:''' Append {{mono|&refdiff_inline=1}} (inline modified changes) or {{mono|&refdiff_inline=0}} (decoupled modified rows; also accepts legacy {{mono|&refdiff_separate=0|1}}) to any diff URL to test without changing your configuration.
* '''Persistent Storage:''' Configure via browser console:
  <syntaxhighlight lang="javascript">
  mw.storage.set('refdiff-inline-modified', 'true');
  </syntaxhighlight>

{| class="wikitable"
! Mode !! Unchanged Citations !! Modified Citations !! Added & Deleted Citations !! Citation Rows Below
|-
| '''Full Decoupling''' (Default)<br />{{mono|inlineModified: false}}
| Collapsed into mathematical badges ({{mono|⟨ref1⟩}} / {{mono|⟨Castritius 2005⟩}}) with hover preview.
| Badged ({{mono|⟨~ref2~⟩}}) and decoupled into separate row below.
| Badged ({{mono|⟨+ref3+⟩}} / {{mono|⟨-ref4-⟩}}) and decoupled into separate row below.
| Yes (one isolated diff row per modified, added, or deleted citation).
|-
| '''Inline Modified Refs'''<br />{{mono|inlineModified: true}}
| Collapsed into mathematical badges ({{mono|⟨ref1⟩}} / {{mono|⟨Castritius 2005⟩}}) with hover preview.
| Badged in prose ({{mono|⟨~ref2~⟩}}) prepended directly before the inline {{tag|ref}} diff; no separated row below.
| Badged ({{mono|⟨+ref3+⟩}} / {{mono|⟨-ref4-⟩}}) and decoupled into separate row below.
| Only for added/deleted citations (modified citations remain inline in prose with {{mono|⟨~label~⟩}} badge prepended, without row expansion below).
|}

== Themes & Skins ==

RefDiff natively supports all major Wikipedia skins and color schemes:
* '''Vector 2022:''' Full native Light Mode and Dark Mode ({{mono|skin-theme-clientpref-night}}).
* '''OS Dark Mode:''' Automatically responds to operating system dark mode settings.
* '''Vector legacy (2010), Timeless, Monobook, Minerva:''' Fully compatible.

== Quality Assurance & Automated Testing ==

RefDiff is backed by a rigorous four-level test pyramid and quality assurance framework (specified in detail in {{mono|TEST_PLAN.md}} in the project repository):

* '''100% Headless Function Coverage:''' All 71 functions across {{mono|refdiff.js}} are verified with 100% function coverage across 14 modular unit, component, and JSDOM test suites in headless Node.js (99 tests executing in ~250&nbsp;ms).
* '''In-Place DOM Memento Invariance:''' Rigorously tests that DOM mutations adhere to the Memento pattern—retaining live DOM element closures, event listeners (such as {{mono|inlineFormatToggle.js}} and VisualEditor), and restoring native MediaWiki diff tables byte-for-byte upon mode toggling.
* '''Shortened Footnotes & Citation Templates:''' Extensively validates tokenization, parameter parsing, entity decoding, and anchor discovery across {{tlx|sfn}}, {{tlx|r}}, {{tlx|efn}}, and complex nested {{tag|ref}} tags.
* '''High-Density Stress Benchmarking:''' Benchmarked on real-world extreme diffs (e.g. airport destination tables with 114 references and split {{mono|diffchange}} boundaries) to guarantee execution under 50&nbsp;ms without browser lag.
* '''Live Browser Automation (CDP):''' End-to-end browser automation tests verify real MediaWiki DOM integration, three-way OOUI mode transitions, dark mode theming, and native {{mono|Extension:Popups}} Reference Preview hovercards on live Wikipedia revisions (e.g. [[Special:Diff/1379486498|Odoacer]], [[Special:Diff/1379409916|Zagreb Airport]], [[Special:Diff/1379548357|Zipf's law]], and [[Special:Diff/1380017400|Donnie Brasco]]).

=== What Is Not Covered (Known Limitations & Gaps) ===

While 100% of internal codebase functions are verified, several external edge cases and layout environments are outside current test coverage (tracked in Section 5 of {{mono|TEST_PLAN.md}}):

* '''Malformed or Broken Wikitext:''' Unclosed {{tag|ref}} tags, tags missing closing brackets, or unusual multiline linebreaks inside tags are skipped by the parser and remain untouched in the prose diff without decoupling.
* '''wikidiff2 Token Boundary & Split-Span Analysis:''' Wikipedia's backend {{mono|wikidiff2}} engine frequently breaks single citation tags into multiple disconnected {{tag|ins}} or {{tag|del}} spans separated by whitespace (e.g. {{mono|<ins>&lt;ref name="x"</ins> <ins>/&gt;</ins>}} as seen in [[Special:Diff/1379491398|Kim Domingo]]). While RefDiff automatically merges adjacent split spans and normalizes tag boundaries, comprehensive automated test analysis of arbitrary token segmentation patterns across diverse MediaWiki diff engines remains an ongoing gap.
* '''Nested Transclusions:''' Footnotes wrapped inside complex secondary templates (such as {{tlx|refn}}, {{tlx|sfnp}}, or citations embedded inside infobox templates) are not yet decoupled into scholarly badges.
* '''Differential Prose Invariance Fuzzing:''' While unit and browser integration tests now explicitly verify whitespace-only edits (such as [[Special:Diff/1379470949|Cosmic inflation]]), systematic differential fuzzing comparing arbitrary real-world {{mono|wikidiff2}} word/character split patterns against RefDiff's post-processing DOM is not yet automated. Very subtle non-character edits (e.g. zero-width spaces, punctuation adjustments, or whitespace directly abutting citation tags) require ongoing regression tracking.
* '''Mobile Diff Layouts (MinervaNeue):''' Responsive single-column stacked diff tables on Wikipedia's mobile view are not currently part of the automated layout test suite (RefDiff is optimized primarily for desktop two-column diffs).
* '''Dynamic AJAX Diff Pagination:''' Successive rapid diff updates fired by live script reloads or interactive history navigation without a full page refresh.
